sources.source: KIP-618: Exactly-Once Support for Source Connectors

items.item: The framework should be expanded to atomically write source records and their source offsets to Kafka, and to prevent zombie tasks from producing data to Kafka

exactly.once.source.support controls whether to enable exactly-once support for source connectors in the cluster by writing source records and their offsets in a Kafka transaction, and by proactively fencing out old task generations before bringing up new ones
Currently, Debezium does not implement an internal deduplication layer to enforce exactly-once semantics

items.item: A logical slot will emit each change just once in normal operation; the current position is persisted only at checkpoint, so a crash can cause recent changes to be sent again, and clients are responsible for handling the same message more than once

at.step: Reveal: the crash and replay, measured

items.item: The crash-and-replay measurement reads the identical pending batch twice with nothing advanced between the two reads, rather than simulating a restart by reconnecting only, so the proof isolates the unmoved position itself as the cause, not any artifact of closing and reopening a connection.

at.step: Reveal: the crash and replay, measured

items.item: The committed-in-time contrast runs against a freshly created slot and table, not the same slot already read from in the crash scenario, so the empty second read proves the position moved, not merely that a different slot happened to have nothing pending.

at.step: Reveal: the crash and replay, measured

items.item: The naive-versus-dedup measurement runs both readers over the exact same duplicated stream produced by one crash scenario, so the contrast is the same input's two different outcomes, not two separately constructed inputs that might differ for unrelated reasons.

The dedup reader keys on each change's own log position rather than on the row's own primary key, which is the detail that actually matters: deduping by primary key would also collapse two separate, legitimate updates to the same row into one.

The purged-position measurement drops the slot entirely rather than merely advancing it far past the data, so the failure it reproduces is specifically an unrecoverable position, not the ordinary and expected case of a slot with nothing new to report.

The wrong option in the first predict question — that the restart skips the already-produced batch — is ruled out by the measured mechanism itself: nothing in a peek-only read ever records that a batch was sent, so there is nothing for a restart to consult in order to skip it.

The wrong option in the final predict question — that enabling exactly-once source support protects the whole pipeline end to end — is ruled out directly by Debezium's own documented no-dedup-layer statement, which draws the boundary at the connector's own write, not at whatever reads from its output topic.

Every scratch table and replication slot this topic creates is confirmed dropped inside the same function that created it, verified by three successive clean runs of examples.py, and the shared orders table is never touched by any of this topic's four functions.
